lines.text: Poison, in a frown? Among the most poisonous substances known, by the nanogram.
lines.phonemes: pˈɔɪzən, ɪn ɐ fɹˈaʊn? ɐmˌʌŋ ðə mˈəʊst pˈɔɪzənəs sˈʌbstənsɪz nˈəʊn, baɪ ðə nˌanəʊɡɹˈam.

lines.text: Every frown starts at a nerve ending, which lets out a chemical messenger onto the muscle below. The muscle pulls, and the skin above it folds into a crease.
lines.phonemes: ˈɛvɹɪ fɹˈaʊn stˈɑːts atə nˈɜːv ˈɛndɪŋ, wˌɪtʃ lˈɛts ˈaʊt ɐ kˈɛmɪkəl mˈɛsɪndʒəɹ ˌɒntʊ ðə mˈʌsəl bɪlˈəʊ. ðə mˈʌsəl pˈʊlz, and ðə skˈɪn əbˌʌv ɪt fˈəʊldz ˌɪntʊ ɐ kɹˈiːs.

lines.text: Botulinum toxin never touches the skin. It slips inside the nerve ending and cuts one small protein the message needs, so the message is ready, and never leaves.
lines.phonemes: bˌɒtjʊlˈaɪnəm tˈɒksɪn nˈɛvə tˈʌtʃɪz ðə skˈɪn. ɪt slˈɪps ɪnsˈaɪd ðə nˈɜːv ˈɛndɪŋ and kˈʌts wˈɒn smˈɔːl pɹˈəʊtiːn ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ nˈiːdz, sˌəʊ ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ ɪz ɹˈɛdi, and nˈɛvə lˈiːvz.

lines.text: Two centuries ago, a German doctor named Justinus Kerner traced a deadly paralysis to spoiled sausages. And he guessed that the same poison might one day become a medicine.
lines.phonemes: tˈuː sˈɛntʃəɹiz ɐɡˈəʊ, ɐ dʒˈɜːmən dˈɒktə nˈeɪmd jʊstˈiːnʊs kˈɛɐnɐ tɹˈeɪst ɐ dˈɛdli pəɹˈaləsˌɪs tə spˈɔɪld sˈɒsɪdʒɪz. and hiː ɡˈɛst ðatðə sˈeɪm pˈɔɪzən mˌaɪt wˈɒn dˈeɪ bɪkˌʌm ɐ mˈɛdsən.

lines.text: So how much goes in? The whole frown takes well under a hundredth of the amount estimated to kill a person.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ hˌaʊ mˈʌtʃ ɡəʊz ˈɪn? ðə hˈəʊl fɹˈaʊn tˈeɪks wˈɛl ˌʌndəɹ ɐ hˈʌndɹədθ ɒvðɪ ɐmˈaʊnt ˈɛstɪmˌeɪtɪd tə kˈɪl ɐ pˈɜːsən.

lines.text: And the gap that message never crosses is about two thousand times thinner than a sheet of paper.
lines.phonemes: and ðə ɡˈap ðat mˈɛsɪdʒ nˈɛvə kɹˈɒsɪz ɪz ɐbˌaʊt tˈuː θˈaʊzənd tˈaɪmz θˈɪnə ðˌanə ʃˈiːt ɒv pˈeɪpə.

lines.text: Poison in a frown: just enough to silence one message, until the nerve grows new endings.
lines.phonemes: pˈɔɪzən ɪn ɐ fɹˈaʊn: dʒˈʌst ɪnˈʌf tə sˈaɪləns wˈɒn mˈɛsɪdʒ, ʌntˈɪl ðə nˈɜːv ɡɹˈəʊz njˈuː ˈɛndɪŋz.

lines.text: Next: two neighbours under the same sun, one experiment. Which hand aged?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: tˈuː nˈeɪbəz ˌʌndə ðə sˈeɪm sˈʌn, wˈɒn ɛkspˈɛɹɪmənt. wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd?
